title: Best Run of Daily Profits
statement:
You are given a chronological list of integers, where each value represents the net profit or loss recorded on a particular day. A *run* is any contiguous stretch of one or more consecutive days.

Your task is to determine the largest possible total you can obtain by summing the values within a single contiguous run. In other words, find the contiguous run of days whose combined profit/loss is as large as possible, and return that maximum total.

The list is guaranteed to contain at least one day, so a valid run always exists (even if every day is a loss, you must still pick at least one day).

Design an efficient solution, a full re-scan for every possible run is not efficient enough for large inputs. Think about how a running best-so-far value, or a divide-and-conquer split of the timeline into halves, can help you avoid redundant recomputation.

examples.explanation: The run [4, -2, 5, -3, 6] sums to 4 + (-2) + 5 + (-3) + 6 = 10, which is higher than any other contiguous stretch, including extending further to include -8.
Every day is a loss, so the best you can do is pick the single least-bad day, -1, since combining any two or more days only makes the total worse.
